narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: The evangelist telling the Passion and Resurrection; grave, steady.

jesus.name: Jesus
jesus.note: The Lord in his Passion and risen; calm, sovereign, tender with his own.

soldiers.name: Soldiers
soldiers.note: The cohort and temple servants sent to arrest Jesus, and the soldiers of Pilate; curt, mocking.

peter.name: Simon Peter
peter.note: Apostle; fearful in his denials, humbled and earnest by the lake.

servant-girl.name: The portress
servant-girl.note: Maid keeping the door of the high priest; a pointed challenge.

high-priests-servant.name: Servant of the high priest
high-priests-servant.note: An attendant standing by who strikes Jesus; indignant.

bystanders.name: Servants at the fire
bystanders.note: Servants and ministers warming themselves in the courtyard; suspicious.

malchus-kinsman.name: Kinsman of Malchus
malchus-kinsman.note: Servant of the high priest, relative of the man Peter wounded; accusing.

the-jews.name: The Jews
the-jews.note: The accusers gathered before the governor's hall; insistent, shouting.

1.t: When Jesus had said these things, he went forth with his disciples over the brook Cedron, where there was a garden, into which he entered with his disciples.

2.t: And Judas also, who betrayed him, knew the place: because Jesus had often resorted thither together with his disciples.

3.t: Judas therefore having received a band of soldiers and servants from the chief priests and the Pharisees, cometh thither with lanterns and torches and weapons.

4.t: Jesus therefore, knowing all things that should come upon him, went forth and said to them:

5.t: And Judas also, who betrayed him, stood with them.

6.t: As soon therefore as he had said to them:

6.q: narrator repeating the words Jesus just spoke; given to his voice

6.t: they went backward and fell to the ground.

8.t: I have told you that I am he. If therefore you seek me, let these go their way,

9.t: That the word might be fulfilled which he said:
Of them whom thou hast given me, I have not lost any one.
9.q: evangelist citing an earlier saying of Jesus (17:12); given to his voice rather than narrator

10.t: Then Simon Peter, having a sword, drew it and struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his right ear. And the name of thee servant was Malchus.

11.t: Put up thy sword into the scabbard. The chalice which my father hath given me, shall I not drink it?

12.t: Then the band and the tribune and the servants of the Jews took Jesus and bound him.

13.t: And they led him away to Annas first, for he was father-in-law to Caiphas, who was the high priest of that year.

14.t: Now Caiphas was he who had given the counsel to the Jews: That it was expedient that one man should die for the people.

15.t: And Simon Peter followed Jesus: and so did another disciple. And that disciple was known to the high priest and went in with Jesus into the court of the high priest.

16.t: But Peter stood at the door without. The other disciple therefore, who was known to the high priest, went out and spoke to the portress and brought in Peter.

17.t: The maid therefore that was portress saith to Peter:
Art not thou also one of this man's disciple?

18.t: Now the servants and ministers stood at a fire of coals, because it was cold, and warmed themselves. And with them was Peter also, standing and warming himself.

19.t: The high priest therefore asked Jesus of his disciples and of his doctrine.

20.t: I have spoken openly to the world. I have always taught in the synagogue and in the temple, whither all the Jews resort: and in secret I have spoken nothing.

21.t: Why askest thou me? Ask them who have heard what I have spoken unto them. Behold they know what things I have said.

22.t: And when he had said these things, one of the servants standing by gave Jesus a blow, saying:
Answerest thou the high priest so?

23.t: If I have spoken evil, give testimony of the evil; but if well, why strikest thou me?

24.t: And Annas sent him bound to Caiphas the high priest.

25.t: And Simon Peter was standing and warming himself. They said therefore to him:
Art not thou also one of his disciples?

26.t: One of the servants of the high priest (a kinsman to him whose ear Peter cut off) saith to him:
Did not I see thee in the garden with him?

27.t: Again therefore Peter denied: and immediately the cock crew.

28.t: Then they led Jesus from Caiphas to the governor's hall. And it was morning: and they went not into the hall, that they might not be defiled, but that they might eat the pasch.

29.t: Pilate therefore went out to them, and said:
What accusation bring you against this man?

30.t: They answered and said to him:
If he were not a malefactor, we would not have delivered him up to thee.

31.t: Take him you, and judge him according to your law.
The Jews therefore said to him:
It is not lawful for us to put any man to death.

32.t: That the word of Jesus might be fulfilled, which he said, signifying what death he should die.

33.t: Pilate therefore went into the hall again and called Jesus and said to him:
Art thou the king of the Jews?

34.t: Sayest thou this thing of thyself, or have others told it thee of me?

35.t: Am I a Jew? Thy own nation and the chief priests have delivered thee up to me. What hast thou done?

36.t: My kingdom is not of this world. If my kingdom were of this world, my servants would certainly strive that I should not be delivered to the Jews: but now my kingdom is not from hence.

37.t: Thou sayest that I am a king. For this was I born, and for this came I into the world; that I should give testimony to the truth. Every one that is of the truth heareth my voice.

38.t: And when he said this, he went out again to the Jews and saith to them:
I find no cause in him.

39.t: But you have a custom that I should release one unto you at the Pasch. Will you, therefore, that I release unto you the king of the Jews?

40.t: Then cried they all again, saying:
